# Engine bundle layout

Each release publishes one engine bundle per platform:
`yadorilink-engine-<channel>-<target>.zip`, with a `.sha256` file and a
provenance statement next to it. A bundle holds exactly the files listed here
for its target and nothing else. Paths are relative to the zip root, use `/`,
and carry no directory entries. The layouts are defined in `LAYOUTS` in
`build-engine-bundle.py`; `verify --target <target>` rejects a bundle with a
missing or extra file.

Every bundle also holds these five files at the root:

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `LICENSE` | License text of the shipped binaries. |
| `SOURCE.txt` | Corresponding source: the public repository, the exact commit SHA the bundle was built from, the release tag, the `build_config_digest` (and the build settings it covers), the layout document, and how to obtain the source. Deterministic; it names the same commit and digest as `engine-identity.json`, and `verify` checks that. |
| `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES` | Plain-text notice for the third-party crates compiled into this bundle's programs (first-party crates left out), grouped by license text, with each text in full. Generated by `generate-third-party-licenses.sh` (cargo-about, `.config/about/about.toml`) for this platform's packages: daemon and CLI everywhere, plus the client facade on Windows and macOS and the shell extension on Windows. Produced in the unprivileged `engine-build` job and passed to `build` with `--third-party-licenses`. |
| `SHA256SUMS` | `<sha256>  <path>` for every file in the bundle except `SHA256SUMS` and `engine-identity.json`, sorted by path. |
| `engine-identity.json` | Engine identity (`.github/checks/engine-identity.schema.json`). `kind` is `release` for the stable and beta channels and `dev` for the dev channel; a `dev` bundle is for development only and every release or production path refuses it (`validate-engine-identity.py --release`, `build-engine-bundle.py verify --release`). `bundle_sha256` is the SHA-256 of `SHA256SUMS`, so it covers every other file, `SOURCE.txt` and `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES` included. `artifact_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the daemon listed below. |

The programs of the bundle (the executables and the client facade library) are compiled with the release id (`<public_commit_sha>:<build_config_digest>`, printed by `build-engine-bundle.py release-id`) in `YADORILINK_RELEASE_ID` and the channel in `YADORILINK_CHANNEL`, so each names its own build without reading `engine-identity.json`. `build` refuses a bundle in which one of them does not contain that id; `check-engine-artifact.py --require-embedded-id` checks that the daemon reports the identity's own id.

Verification only hashes: the zip against its `.sha256`, each file against
`SHA256SUMS`, `SHA256SUMS` against `bundle_sha256`, and the daemon against
`artifact_sha256`. Nothing from a bundle is run before those hashes match. The
zip is deterministic (sorted entries, fixed timestamps, fixed modes: `0755` for
executables, `0644` otherwise).

## linux-x86_64

```
yadorilink
yadorilink-daemon          (artifact_sha256)
```

## windows-x86_64

All files are at the root.

```
yadorilink.exe
yadorilink-daemon.exe      (artifact_sha256)
yadorilink_shell_ext.dll   Explorer overlay and context-menu extension
yadorilink-cfapi-host.exe  Cloud Files sync-root host
yadorilink_client_ffi.dll  client facade library the Windows app loads
csharp/BINDING-NOTES.md    generator, UniFFI and API-surface versions, how to use the binding
csharp/Generated/*.cs      generated C# binding (one or more files)
```

The shell extension and CfAPI host (`yadorilink_shell_ext.dll`,
`yadorilink-cfapi-host.exe`) are built from `crates/yadorilink-shell-ext-windows`
(its own Cargo workspace, `cargo build --release --manifest-path crates/yadorilink-shell-ext-windows/Cargo.toml`, output under that crate's `target/release`); the rest from the main
workspace.

The client facade library is `cargo build --release -p yadorilink-client-ffi`.
Cargo produces `yadorilink_client_ffi.dll`, the name the generated C# loads and the bundle ships. The C# binding is generated at bundle build time from that
same DLL (`.github/release/generate-csharp-binding.sh --library DLL --out DIR`,
the `csharp` root); nothing is checked in except its API surface snapshot
(`csharp-api-surface.txt`), which the generator checks. The generated code
refuses to load a library whose API checksums differ, so a binding and a
library from different builds cannot be mixed. The generator is
`uniffi-bindgen-cs`, pinned in `csharp-bindgen.pin`. It is MPL-2.0: each
generated file starts with the MPL-2.0 notice (generator, version, source), and
`csharp/BINDING-NOTES.md` states the generator, its pinned commit, its licence
and where its source is.

## macos-aarch64

```
bin/yadorilink
bin/yadorilink-daemon                         (artifact_sha256)
lib/libyadorilink_client_ffi.a                static library the app links
swift/Generated/YadoriLinkCore.swift          generated Swift binding
swift/Generated/YadoriLinkFFI.swift
swift/Generated/include/*.h                   generated C headers (one or more)
swift/Generated/include/module.modulemap      one clang module per header
ipc-proto/proto/shellipc.proto                shell IPC schema
ipc-proto/src/framing.rs                      shell IPC framing
```

The Swift binding is generated at bundle build time, from the library in the
same bundle (`.github/release/generate-swift-binding.sh --out DIR`); nothing
is checked in. The macOS app repository consumes it from the bundle.

## The engine.lock release asset

Next to each zip the release publishes `engine.lock.<target>.json`, the
per-target lock a consumer pins (Apple `Engine/update-pin.sh`, the Windows
`engine.lock`). It is the verified bundle's `engine-identity.json`, byte for
byte what `build-engine-bundle.py lock` writes: `kind` is `release`, the
`source` object names the public repository, the release tag and the zip's asset
name, and `public_commit_sha` is the commit the tag points at (the engine
identity, not the initial public commit). The `engine-bundle` job writes it with

```
build-engine-bundle.py lock yadorilink-engine-<channel>-<target>.zip --target <target> --public-commit-sha <tagged commit> [--release] --out-dir DIR
```

after the hash re-verification and provenance; `lock` refuses an unverified or
tampered zip, a layout or commit that does not match, and (with `--release`) a
development bundle. `build-engine-bundle.py verify ZIP --lock FILE --release`
checks a downloaded lock against its zip. The development engine release uses the same file
name with `kind: dev`.

## Trust chain

The release workflow builds each bundle in three jobs with separate privileges:

1. `engine-build` (read-only token, no environment, no secrets) builds the
   binaries, runs the pinned third-party binding generators and uploads the
   zip and its `.sha256`. It holds no `id-token` or `attestations` permission.
2. `engine-attest` (`contents: read`, `id-token: write`, `attestations: write`;
   no environment, secrets, generator or build step) downloads only this run's
   `engine-build-<target>` artifact, re-verifies it by hash (nothing from it
   runs) and creates a GitHub build-provenance attestation for the zip.
3. `engine-bundle` (the protected release environment) first runs
   `gh attestation verify` on the downloaded zip, pinned to
   `github.repository`, its `.github/workflows/release.yml`, the commit
   (`--source-digest`) and the ref. The check fails closed: no attestation, a
   different signer or a different source commit stops the job, and the zip's
   digest must equal the attestation subject's. Only then does it re-verify by
   hash and write the provenance statement, which records the attestation's
   signer workflow, source repository, commit and ref (`attestation` object).

`check-release-gates.py` enforces this structure. Limits: the attestation
proves that this repository's release workflow, at that commit, produced these
exact bytes. It does not show that the generators run in `engine-build` were
harmless; their pins and the hash and layout verification are what bound that
risk. GitHub artifact attestations need a public repository, or a GitHub
Enterprise Cloud plan for a private or internal one; on other plans the
`engine-attest` job fails and no bundle is produced.
